races.name: JenningsBet In North Shields Handicap

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Mrs R Carr returning off 20 days; one placing from seven attempts on similar going tempers confidence, though a drop back to handicap company at this trip gives a chance to find her level.

runners_data.name: Fanjove
runners_data.note: Won on Standard over 7f at Newcastle and has a strong similar-going record of two wins and five places from twelve; S De Sousa's booking for an Dunlop three-year-old with proven course-and-distance form is a significant angle.

runners_data.name: Saxon Prince
runners_data.note: Trainer J & S Quinn in solid 14-day form (3/17); this horse is at heart a hold-up type whose true style is at the back, though 70 days off and five failures to win on Standard going are legitimate concerns in a race where closers need pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Elemma
runners_data.note: Three runs only, all on Good at Goodwood — the step to Standard to Slow at Newcastle is an unknown quantity; a natural closer by inclination whose redistribution to midfield means she will not settle in her habitual deep position.

runners_data.name: Smartanck
runners_data.note: Has won twice over a mile at Newcastle on Standard going and wears a tongue-tie; dropping back to 7f is the query, but course familiarity and a record that holds up on this surface make her a realistic player if the race unfolds in a messy fashion.

runners_data.name: Bird Of War
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on Standard for Charlie Hills and has been placed at this course; true hold-up nature means the field's pace excess forces her out of her comfort zone, and two runs on Good ground this season suggests she handles variety, though similar-going figures are modest (1 win, 1 place from 8).

runners_data.name: Rousham
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner for Faye McManoman and N Tinkler; won over 7f on Good at Goodwood and placed over 6f, but has zero wins or places from five similar-going attempts — the uncontested lead flatters her raw ability, and the headgear (hood) adds a settling angle.

runners_data.name: Henriette Ronner
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard for the Coyle & Wood yard but is by instinct a hold-up racer pushed into midfield by the field's excess of closers; 11 days since last run and a poor recent form string (714950) mean fitness and consistency are both questions.

runners_data.name: Secretinthesky
runners_data.note: Miss J A Camacho's runner has only three career runs and no wins or places on similar going; this genuine backmarker is placed in midfield through redistribution and has little course-and-distance evidence to lean on, making her one of the bigger unknowns in the field.

runners_data.name: Popty Ping
runners_data.note: D O'Meara's in-form yard (8/54 in 14 days) send out Popty Ping wearing a visor; an excellent similar-going record (2 wins, 8 places from 15 runs) and a natural prominent style make this horse one of the best-placed to capitalise on the single-pacemaker dynamic, able to stalk Rousham and strike.

runners_data.name: Based
runners_data.note: Won his penultimate start over 7f at Newcastle on Standard going — that course-and-distance win is the standout credential in this field; though a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield by the map's redistribution, his Newcastle familiarity and recent winning form give him genuine claims if any pace develops.

runners_data.name: Maynora
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's four-year-old has winning form over 6f on Soft for the yard and goes 10 days after last run; genuine closer by inclination mapped to midfield given the field's structural imbalance, and the step up to 7f on Standard is a slight unknown given a record that trends shorter.

runners_data.name: Surgeon Commander
runners_data.note: Lidster's second string also wears a hood and has won twice on Standard; his best form has come over shorter trips and his similar-going record (2W, 3P from 11) is solid, but as a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield he needs a pace that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Strong Voice
runners_data.note: P J McDonald takes the mount on James Horton's runner after a 75-day absence; placed twice on Standard over 7f, which is encouraging, but the lengthy break and a form string of 34-0 leave fitness very much the key question — if fit, the class angle is slight given a topweight assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Rousham is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine rival to press her from flag to flag, she is likely to control the pace from a handy position without being harassed — creating a sustainable, honest gallop on Standard to Slow ground rather than a searingly fast one. Popty Ping is the only other legitimate prominent horse, so those two will share the early real estate up front while the remainder of the field, dominated by hold-up types, fan out behind them. The field contains a significant excess of hold-up horses — Saxon Prince, Elemma, Bird Of War, Henriette Ronner, Secretinthesky, Based, Maynora and Surgeon Commander are all genuine closers who cannot all obtain their natural rear-of-field position, meaning several will be shuffled into an uncharacteristic midfield station. A controlled, single-pacemaker scenario on a flat track over 7f heavily favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce without needing a wall of pace to run through; pure hold-up types are disadvantaged because the gallop is unlikely to be fast enough to string the field out and create the gaps they need late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rousham Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Rousham dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough momentum from the rear to reel in those forward.
scenarios.body: Rousham sets a sensible tempo on the Standard to Slow surface, leaving Popty Ping ideally placed to track her through the first half before challenging in the final two furlongs; horses ridden prominently are handed the race on a plate as closers find the pace insufficient to close the gap. Fanjove, who has winning form at 7f on Standard and possesses fine course form, is positioned to stalk and strike from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rousham's unchallenged lead gives her enough in reserve to sustain her effort through the final furlong and the hold-up brigade arrive too late.
scenarios.body: If Rousham's unchallenged lead gives her enough in reserve to sustain her effort through the final furlong and the hold-up brigade arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horse Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the field is sufficiently strung out to create room for a genuine closer to weave through.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the field is sufficiently strung out to create room for a genuine closer to weave through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If crowding at the break or a mid-race accident reshuffles the field entirely and the race devolves into a rough, uneven contest.
scenarios.body: If crowding at the break or a mid-race accident reshuffles the field entirely and the race devolves into a rough, uneven contest.

watchPoints.text: Popty Ping is ideally positioned as the only prominent type capable of tracking Rousham; if D O'Meara's horse jumps cleanly and settles just behind the leader in a single-pacemaker race, he is the horse most likely to inherit the race in the final two furlongs.

Rousham must be monitored from the stalls — if she breaks cleanly and immediately establishes herself on the front end without challenge, her uncontested lead on Standard to Slow ground becomes a serious tactical weapon that the hold-up brigade will struggle to overcome.

Based won over 7f at Newcastle on Standard on his most recent winning run and could be dangerously fresh off 23 days; despite being displaced into midfield through redistribution, a horse with proven course-and-distance winning form must not be written off if he manoeuvres to a prominent enough position early.

With eight or more genuine hold-up types unable to settle in their natural rear position, watch for crowding and interference in the middle of the field in the opening two furlongs — horses like Henriette Ronner, Secretinthesky and Elemma, forced to race out of role, increase the risk of a compressed, scrimmaging pack.

Fanjove's jockey booking (S De Sousa) for a Dunlop yard with 1/14 in the 14-day window deserves respect — the horse's 7f Newcastle win on Standard is a direct match for today's conditions, and a prominent ride from De Sousa could put him in an ideal stalking position behind Rousham.

races.name: JenningsBet In Scarborough Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Eternal Force
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with a strong winning sequence (three on the bounce) though the two most recent form figures of 7 and 2 suggest the class rise and step up from 8f to 10f is being tested; Haggas yard in excellent 14-day form (9/41), but this horse is mapping slightly out of role as a pace-setter rather than prominent tracker — the controlled tempo it creates benefits it most if rivals are content to let it bowl along.

runners_data.name: Will Scarlet
runners_data.note: Has a strong course-and-distance profile at 1m2f on Good and similar, with a win and three places from four similar-going runs; Crisford yard quiet at 1/20 in 14 days and 43 days between runs may require a forward showing, but the prominent style suits perfectly in a race with a single controlled pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Outstanding record on Standard going — 15 from 15 runs, five wins and eight places — makes the surface switch from his recent Good-ground races almost irrelevant if the ground matches his optimum; the 148-day absence is the one flag, but the Loughnane yard is at 0/21 in the last fortnight which tempers confidence, and this horse simply thrives on this type of surface.

runners_data.name: Whitcombe Rockstar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has back-to-back wins at 12f and 11f on Standard, giving her solid place form on this surface (9/15, 2W4P); the tongue-tie is retained, she was out just 13 days ago suggesting fitness, and from a wide draw she will need the pace to genuinely lift in the straight rather than finish in a procession.

runners_data.name: Rogue Millions
runners_data.note: Prominent-style four-year-old who has won on both Soft and Good going but has only one placing from seven on Standard — a notable surface concern at this track; the Bethell yard has been in decent recent nick (4/25) and at OR 94 this is a competitive mark, but the Standard going record is thin.

runners_data.name: Jolly Jack Tar
runners_data.note: Returning from 331 days off for the Gosden yard (7/36 in 14 days, solid), with a good Standard going record of 2W4P from five runs at 10f, suggesting the trip and surface are not problems; the long absence is the obvious risk, but if the Gosden team have him ready to run his race he could outrun his odds tracking prominently.

runners_data.name: The Glen Rovers
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old who is genuinely prominent-natured but cannot secure that position in this traffic-heavy field; his best form on Standard going is substantial (6W7P from 15 runs at 10f+), and Sean Bowen's booking is interesting, but being pushed back from his preferred spot is a real handicap to his chance here.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners_data.note: A four-year-old who wants to race prominently and has won twice, including on Standard, but is being squeezed back by sheer weight of pace — his best form figures on Standard going (1W4P from 12 runs) are acceptable rather than outstanding, and Fentiman's 3lb claim helps on weight but not on position.

runners_data.name: Cloth Of Gold
runners_data.note: Johnston-trained four-year-old with a win and three places from six Standard-going runs, including a win at 10f on Standard; like Rainbow Nebula and The Glen Rovers, this horse is naturally prominent but the density of the pace group means it cannot get a clean run from the front — the 13-day turnaround suggests freshness but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Style unknown (tagged U), making scenario modelling difficult; the going record on Standard is blank from six runs (0W0P) and the Jardine yard has been active, but this is the least data-rich profile in the race — worth watching early to see whether she goes forward or settles back.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a poor record on Standard going (1W2P from 15 runs) and mediocre recent form (-97034); the Easterby yard is busy at 7/98 in 14 days though that volume suggests quantity over quality, and the tongue tie is retained — the going record is a genuine concern for any late-run scenario.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Non-runner — no analysis applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Force is the lone confirmed front runner and, with only one horse actively seeking to lead, is set to control the pace from the front on what will be a Standard to Slow surface at Newcastle's flat, galloping track — a setup that typically rewards those who can dictate without being harassed. With Haku, Will Scarlet, and Rogue Millions all prominent-style horses who will seek to sit close to the pace, there is enough secondary pressure to keep Eternal Force honest, but none of those horses are likely to actively take on the lead, meaning the fractions will be measured rather than frenetic. The Glen Rovers, Rainbow Nebula, and Cloth Of Gold are genuine prominent types who cannot all secure that position in a field this loaded with pace-minded runners, and one or more will be forced to settle in a midfield role that does not suit their natural style — most likely The Glen Rovers and Rainbow Nebula will be squeezed back given Cloth Of Gold's inside draw angle. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind a single, controlled pacer and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — hold-up horses will need an unusually strong gallop that is unlikely to materialise, making true closers a low-probability profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eternal Force Controls, Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Force is permitted to roll along at a measured pace without serious challenge and the Standard to Slow ground blunts late closers.
scenarios.body: If Eternal Force is permitted to roll along at a measured pace without serious challenge and the Standard to Slow ground blunts late closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Force's front-running role creates a pressured enough tempo from the pack behind that a prominent chaser picks up and nails it close home.
scenarios.body: If Eternal Force's front-running role creates a pressured enough tempo from the pack behind that a prominent chaser picks up and nails it close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the secondary prominent group sets a stronger-than-expected pace chasing Eternal Force, genuinely softening the race up for those ridden patiently.
scenarios.body: If the secondary prominent group sets a stronger-than-expected pace chasing Eternal Force, genuinely softening the race up for those ridden patiently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Shape, Chaotic Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of The Glen Rovers, Rainbow Nebula, and Cloth Of Gold produces early positional scrimmaging that elevates the pace and scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution of The Glen Rovers, Rainbow Nebula, and Cloth Of Gold produces early positional scrimmaging that elevates the pace and scrambles the race shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Haku's 148-day absence combined with trainer Loughnane's 0/21 14-day strike rate is a live fitness flag — watch the market move and early behaviour in the paddock, because on paper his Standard-going record is the strongest in the race.

The Glen Rovers, Rainbow Nebula, and Cloth Of Gold are all genuinely prominent in style but cannot all get their position — watch the first two furlongs for scrimmaging as these three negotiate their roles, as any early incident or checking could compromise multiple fancies simultaneously.

Eternal Force's recent form figures of 7 and 2 (after three consecutive wins) suggest it may be at or near its ceiling — if the pace collapses rather than sustains into the final quarter-mile, Tom Marquand's positional choices in the last half-furlong will be critical.

Jolly Jack Tar returns from 331 days off — watch for Gosden-stable market moves late on and note whether the horse is sent off at a price that reflects a fitness run or a genuine tilt, given the trainer's 7/36 14-day record signals active, winning form.

Standard to Slow going (confirmed in the race-day report) is slower than the headline Standard suggests — horses with deep, proven form on genuinely slow surfaces (Haku, Whitcombe Rockstar, The Glen Rovers) may receive a hidden advantage over those whose Standard going record is limited or absent.

races.name: JenningsBet In Kippax Seaton Delaval Handicap

runners_data.name: Treble Tee
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with an OR of 103 at the top of the weights; last run was 89 days ago which is the principal concern, but S & E Crisford horses return fit, and the style-fit flag here is marginal given this is effectively a lead role in context — the key question is whether the layoff blunts the finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Al Mubhir
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides a hold-up specialist whose recent form string of 500-05 is sobering, but six of his last seven starts have been on Good ground and the move to Standard To Slow at Newcastle on turf suits better than those figures suggest — needs the race to set up late.

runners_data.name: Ancient Rome
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes over on a hold-up type whose last five starts show a pattern of finishing mid-pack on Good ground; dropping back from ten furlongs to a mile and switching to Standard To Slow asks new questions of a seven-year-old who has not won since 2022.

runners_data.name: Back In Black
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt partners a consistent prominent racer for Fanshawe who has finished in the first four in four of his last five; the synthetic-going marker (1 win from 11) is worth flagging on this Newcastle surface, though his Goodwood form on turf is more encouraging than that stat implies.

runners_data.name: Dosman
runners_data.note: Oli Rix's five-year-old has a superb record at around this trip on Standard and Standard To Slow going — nine outings, one win, six places — and Jonny Peate fits the lightweight claim well; a natural prominent type whose sim-going figures are the most compelling in the field.

runners_data.name: Mr Swivell
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner for De Foy whose trainer has sent out zero winners in the last 14 days from 12 runners, which is a cold flag; his best form came on Soft going and his record on Standard surfaces is thin — pace and enthusiasm without the class to go with it here.

runners_data.name: Dingle
runners_data.note: Ryan Sexton partners a genuine hold-up type with a strong Newcastle record — three wins from ten at this course on Standard — and an OR of 90 that looks workable at the weights; the eight-year-old's age is the caveat, but his course-and-distance profile stands out.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old carries a blinker flag and holds an OR of 90 on a career best of 1-0934 recently; in truth a front-runner by nature who is pushed into a midfield map position by the weight of pace in this field — the blinkers may mean he contests the early positions regardless, which could compromise his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: El Matador
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly-framed four-year-old has placed in three of his last five and is progressing, but his sim-going record on Standard is just one placing from nine tries; a horse who naturally wants to race prominently yet finds himself consigned to midfield by circumstance — his chance depends on finding cover without losing too much ground early.

runners_data.name: Clouds Hill
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston has four winners from 34 runners in the past fortnight, a solid strike-rate, and this four-year-old won on Standard at Wolverhampton last time in trip terms; by instinct a pace-pressing type who is squeezed into midfield by the race shape — his better form has come when able to bowl along, and the constraint may blunt his challenge.

runners_data.name: Regalian
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's four-year-old ran just six days ago, which is a notable fitness positive, and carries the lowest weight at 117lbs; by preference a prominent racer but the redistribution means he may find himself further back than ideal — the light weight and quick turnaround give him an angle, though his recent form figures of 2763-6 do not inspire.

races.paceDynamic: Treble Tee is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press them, Mason Paetel can dictate a sustainable, controlled tempo on Standard To Slow ground over Newcastle's flat mile. The field behind is crammed with promoted prominent-types — Christian David, El Matador, Clouds Hill and Regalian are all natural pace-seekers who cannot all find their preferred position and will be shuffled into a midfield queue that is not their true home. This compression behind Treble Tee means the race shape is unlikely to produce a true end-to-end test; instead, a modest early clip followed by a punishing home-straight injection suits those who can travel close to the tempo without burning early energy. The dominant tactical verdict is that genuine hold-up horses and midfield gallopers who possess a turn of foot will struggle against those who can sit second or third to an uncontested leader and pounce when the pace lifts in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Treble Tee Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Treble Tee bowls along without rival pressure and the pace is genuinely steady, those able to track within two lengths of the leader will have first run.
scenarios.body: If Treble Tee bowls along without rival pressure and the pace is genuinely steady, those able to track within two lengths of the leader will have first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Aids Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of redistributed prominent types jostle for cover behind Treble Tee and create a messy middle-race section, genuine hold-up horses can work through late.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of redistributed prominent types jostle for cover behind Treble Tee and create a messy middle-race section, genuine hold-up horses can work through late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Pressured Early
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the natural prominent types refuses to settle and pushes forward to test Treble Tee before halfway, the tempo rises and stamina becomes the deciding factor.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the natural prominent types refuses to settle and pushes forward to test Treble Tee before halfway, the tempo rises and stamina becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl Produces Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Treble Tee crawls and the whole field backs up, an all-out sprint from two furlongs out favours the horse with the highest raw speed on the day.
scenarios.body: If Treble Tee crawls and the whole field backs up, an all-out sprint from two furlongs out favours the horse with the highest raw speed on the day.

watchPoints.text: Dosman — if Jonny Peate can slot him into his natural prominent position just off Treble Tee's shoulder, his Standard-to-Slow sim-going record of nine outings with one win and six places makes him the chief danger to any outcome.

Christian David and El Matador — both are natural pace-seekers mapped out of position; watch the early stages to see whether either attempts to push forward past Treble Tee, as any contest for the lead will significantly alter the tempo and reshape the entire race.

Dingle — at eight years old his winning form at Newcastle on Standard is genuine and Sexton knows the course well; if the prominent types get into a scrap and create a gap on the inside rail in the final two furlongs, he is the most likely horse to exploit it.

Going confirmation — the Standard To Slow description for this 1m contest is firmer than Standard but not Soft; Back In Black's synthetic-going concern and Ancient Rome's string of Good-ground efforts suggest the exact surface may matter more than the headline figure implies, and any late-afternoon watering update should be noted.

races.name: True Colours Charity Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
JenningsBet In Allerdene Handicap

runners_data.name: Ice Cold Alex
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up filly from Ollie Pears's yard with only 2 places from 9 runs on similar going — genuine closer who will be sweeping late but needs the pace to collapse more than it is likely to on this slow-ish surface.

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with a win from this position on soft and good-to-firm; Tom Marquand takes over in the saddle and a visor is fitted, suggesting connections want her to race with more purpose — dictates here if she breaks cleanly.

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed twice from 8 runs on similar going including a win on Standard at Newcastle; lurks with genuine each-way claims if she can find a prominent pitch from her draw given how compressed the closing run looks.

runners_data.name: Brave Traveller
runners_data.note: Won on Standard at this trip and placed on identical going, giving her the best sim-going record of the closers; B Smart's yard out of form (0/9 in 14 days) tempers enthusiasm despite the tactical fit — watch her finishing effort from midfield.

runners_data.name: I'm Dan Dare
runners_data.note: Prominent-style colt fitted with a hood; has won and placed multiple times over this trip at Goodwood — the step to Newcastle on slower going is an unknown but his front-rank racing style suits the pace scenario ideally if he can slot in second or third.

runners_data.name: Record Day
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish and his recent form over 6-7f on good ground offers little encouragement; no wins or places from 5 runs on similar ground and the drop back to 5f looks unlikely to solve his finishing problems.

runners_data.name: Blue Nguru
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who won on Standard going over 5f and showed well at 6f — true closer repositioned into midfield on this map because of traffic; his visor and 37-day break are worth noting, and his style-fit discount means he needs a perfect run if closers are to land.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Placed in a 5f handicap on good ground but has been out of form on this trip recently; a true hold-up horse nudged into midfield by field congestion, and Tim Easterby's yard is processing high volume (8 runners in 14 days) — the pace scenario does not flatter him.

runners_data.name: Slot
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from 5 runs on Standard-to-Slow ground and won on Standard previously, showing genuine aptitude for these conditions; a natural closer working out of an adjusted map position, the lightest realistic weight in the field helps but he needs a much stronger pace than Koffee And Kale is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: Won on Standard going over 5f and placed on Standard-to-Slow, making her one of the better-qualified closers for today's conditions; held up by instinct but pushed into midfield on the map — her 5-10 record on similar going and the Rhys Elliott claim give her an each-way profile if the race sets up.

runners_data.name: The Tunguska Event
runners_data.note: Best recent form of any runner here — two wins and two places from five runs including wins on Standard going — and a visor is worn; a true hold-up horse remapped to midfield because of field congestion, but if he gets his run he has the form to be dangerous and Jason Hart knows him well.

runners_data.name: Bella Delizia
runners_data.note: Prominent-style filly from Nigel Tinkler's yard with a win over 5f on good going, drawn to potentially get an uncontested berth behind the leader; 0/6 on Standard or slower going is a genuine concern and the 3lb claim for Alex Jary is a modest compensation.

runners_data.name: Contorno
runners_data.note: Most lightly weighted runner in the field (OR 56) and has won on Standard going over 5f; a natural closer displaced to midfield, and the 47-day absence for a small Tate operation (0/2 in 14 days) adds risk — but if the race fragments at the start, the weight allowance could make him dangerous.

races.paceDynamic: Koffee And Kale is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to pressure her for the lead, she has every chance of dictating a measured, controlled tempo from the Newcastle 5f gates. The Standard To Slow going (reported consistently across the card) will further compress early fractions, rewarding horses that travel with the pace rather than those required to make sustained ground from off it. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Blue Nguru, Under The Radar, The Tunguska Event, Slot, Love Alive and Contorno are all genuine closers who cannot all find their natural position and several will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts, diluting the closing threat. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace in the first two or three lengths of the leader, as a steady tempo set by one horse on slow-ish ground will not generate the strong pace collapse that pure closers need to swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Koffee And Kale Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Koffee And Kale secures the lead unchallenged and sets a steady, measured tempo that denies closers a true test.
scenarios.body: If Koffee And Kale secures the lead unchallenged and sets a steady, measured tempo that denies closers a true test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Dan Dare or another prominent type pushes up to dispute the lead early, lifting the tempo and turning it into a genuine two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: If I'm Dan Dare or another prominent type pushes up to dispute the lead early, lifting the tempo and turning it into a genuine two-horse duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot enough through the first two furlongs to cause Koffee And Kale to tie up, opening the race for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely hot enough through the first two furlongs to cause Koffee And Kale to tie up, opening the race for hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If there is a slow or fractured start that breaks the race into several small groups racing on different parts of the track.
scenarios.body: If there is a slow or fractured start that breaks the race into several small groups racing on different parts of the track.

watchPoints.text: Koffee And Kale breaks cleanly — if she slopes into the lead without immediate challenge she sets a tempo entirely on her own terms, making her very difficult to reel in on Standard To Slow ground over just 5f.

The Tunguska Event's redistribution from hold-up to midfield could be decisive — if Jason Hart is unable to find a clear passage through a compressed field of 13, his strong recent form may count for nothing despite being the best-credentialed closer in the race.

I'm Dan Dare is the most likely horse to pressurise Koffee And Kale early; if he does push up and the two lock together in the first furlong, the tempo lifts sharply and the entire scenario probability matrix shifts toward Scenario B and away from Scenario A.

Multiple hold-up horses (Blue Nguru, Under The Radar, Slot, Love Alive, The Tunguska Event, Contorno) are all genuine closers compressed into midfield — a wall of finishing horses in the final furlong is likely, raising the risk of interference and a stewards' enquiry.

Standard To Slow going is reported for this race across all updates — any horse with sim-going form on Standard or Slow surfaces (Brave Traveller, Love Alive, The Tunguska Event, Blue Nguru) holds a meaningful edge over rivals whose form is exclusively on good ground.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Hold-up style in form having won two of last six; Roger Fell yard in decent nick (1/6 T14), and similar going suits — best chance for the closers if she gets a clean route through.|

runners_data.name: Oselton

runners_data.name: Barleybrown
runners_data.note: Placed twice in similar going and handles Standard well; a genuine hold-up type whose natural race is from the rear, though the glut of closers in this field means she may find herself tighter for room than ideal — headgear (p) fitted.|

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine campaigns who settles into a hold-up role habitually; T D Easterby sends him out fresh (9d) and headgear (p) is applied, but his sim-going record is modest and he would need a very clean run through the field at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old with an excellent record in similar conditions (11/15 sim-going starts, 1W 3P) and handles Newcastle's straight mile; his natural game is from the back but at his age relies heavily on pace and a gap materialising.|

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner; headgear (p) worn, handled Standard before (1W 2P in sim-going), and with no rival to seriously push her, she should be able to set an unchallenged tempo — the key horse around whom the entire race shape revolves.|

runners_data.name: Abu Royal
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on Standard ground with a placed effort at this trip (3/8f/STA) and a natural hold-up style pushed into a tighter midfield than he would prefer; trainer L Morgan has only one runner in the 14-day window — narrow angle.|

runners_data.note: Strong Standard-ground specialist with 13 out of 14 sim-going runs on that surface and a win over seven furlongs at Newcastle's equivalent; genuine hold-up type who will need to come from behind, but his course familiarity and form figures are the most eye-catching in the field.|

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing sort who has been placed on Standard at seven furlongs; a three-pound claim for Alex Jary is a small bonus and his likely position just off Sassy Glory's pace makes him the most straightforwardly positioned horse in the race.|

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has run creditably at this course before; PJ McDonald is the best jockey in the race, but the horse's true hold-up style means he needs horses ahead to come back to him — sim-going record is thin (4/15).|

runners_data.name: Shimmering Spirit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with modest form and no wins; hold-up style and reasonable Standard-ground record (3/5) but the weight of 127lbs at this level and a form string containing no top-three finishes at a mile make it hard to be enthusiastic.|

runners_data.name: Space Moon
runners_data.note: Another hold-up three-year-old; trainer B Ellison is in form (1/18 T14) and Ben Robinson is a capable claimer's booking, but the horse has no wins and has struggled to get involved at a mile on Good — the slower ground may not help.|

races.paceDynamic: Sassy Glory is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner mile handicap on Standard to Slow ground at Newcastle, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. I Can Boogy is the only other prominent-type likely to race near the pace, giving Sassy Glory a clear lead with minimal immediate pressure. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Barleybrown, Kalikapour, Little Ted, Trais Fluors, Abu Royal, Cable Beach and Mavetheforcebewivu are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers to show at the rear; in practice the trailing pack will be bunched and jostling for position through the first half of the race. A measured, uncontested pace on slow-ish ground over a mile strongly favours a horse that can sit just off the lead in a position of control rather than making up ground from the back of a congested field — prominent or handy runners who track Sassy Glory without getting buried will be best placed when the race quickens in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Sassy Glory is the pivot of this race — if she jumps cleanly and Rhys Elliott does not overcook the pace, she could prove very difficult to reel in against a field of closers stuck in a congested group.|

Cable Beach's course-and-distance form on Standard is the standout data point among the hold-up pack; watch whether Robert Havlin can find a clear route from the rear in the straight, because on figures he has every right to be involved.|

The midfield is dangerously overcrowded with hold-up types — Barleybrown, Little Ted, Abu Royal, Mavetheforcebewivu and others will all be hunting the same gaps in the straight, raising the risk of interference or checked runs for several at once.|

I Can Boogy is the only horse likely to track Sassy Glory at close quarters; if he can hold that position into the straight without over-racing, he becomes the most dangerous immediate threat to the front-runner.|

Woodleigh's last two runs have been wins and she is dropping back from 10 furlongs — watch whether K Stott opts to ride her more prominently than her usual hold-up profile to avoid the traffic problem that will plague the rear of this field.|
